title: oncall-dependency-mapper-and-fallback-fabric
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: during on-call war rooms we repeatedly lose time mapping which downstream services will be impacted and what safe mitigations (rate-limit, proxy fallback, read-only-mode) are viable. This PR adds a lightweight oncall dependency mapper service and a 'fallback fabric' suggestion layer that integrates with incident-bot's runbook recommender so responders get ranked, actionable fallback options alongside evidence. Summary: 1) dep-mapper: agent and aggregator that consumes service topology from service-registry and lightweight span-sampling (optional) to build a real-time dependency graph with health annotations; 2) fallback-fabric: rules engine that synthesizes safe mitigation suggestions (proxy failover, degraded routes, client-side throttles) based on dependency blast radius, traffic patterns, and configured safety policies; 3) incident-bot integration: runbook payloads now include a "Fallback candidates" section with confidence scores and automated rollback notes; 4) config and kill-switches: feature flag + per-team opt-out; 5) observability: new metrics, traces, and a small dashboard added. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for dep graph builder - [x] integration tests for rule engine - [x] e2e local simulation harness - [x] docs/ops guidance and playbook examples - [x] rollout plan and feature flag gating Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserved — suggestions are read-only until operator triggers a mitigation. Security & safety: all automated actions are advisory by default; hard mitigations require explicit oncall confirmation and RBAC check. See linked Linear ENG-7886 for design notes and SUP-3472 for an on-call incident that motivated the feature.
